study.title: Simvastatin Improves Neutrophil Function and Clinical Outcomes in Pneumonia: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
study.authors: Elizabeth Sapey; Jaimin M. Patel; Hannah Greenwood; Georgia M. Walton; Frances Grudzinska; Dhruv Parekh; Rahul Y. Mahida; Rachel C. A. Dancer; Sebastian T. Lugg; Philip A. Howells; Jon Hazeldine; Paul Newby; Aaron Scott; Peter Nightingale; Adam T. Hill; David R. Thickett
study.journal: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
study.design: Single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial
study.study_phase: Pilot proof-of-concept trial (phase not explicitly reported)
study.condition: Community-acquired pneumonia with sepsis in hospitalized adults older than 55 years

master_study_rows: Single-center, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot trial
Pilot proof-of-concept trial (phase not explicitly reported)
Simvastatin Improves Neutrophil Function and Clinical Outcomes in Pneumonia: A Pilot Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
Community-acquired pneumonia with sepsis in hospitalized adults older than 55 years

arms.label: Simvastatin 80 mg plus standard pneumonia treatment

eligibility.qualifier: diagnosis of community-acquired pneumonia per British Thoracic Society definition
meet the criteria for sepsis on the basis of the 2012 Surviving Sepsis Campaign guidelines
written informed consent or assent from a personal or professional legal representative
More than 48 h from admission at time of consent
current or recent high-dose statin use within 1 mo
known prior myositis or a family history of muscular disorders
Creatine kinase >10 times upper limit of normal
Transaminases (ALT/AST) >8 times upper limit of normal
severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <30 ml/min) not receiving renal replacement therapy
ongoing sustained treatment with prohibited CYP3A4 inhibitors or interacting medicines listed in Table 1
known HIV or hepatitis B or C virus infection
contraindication to enteral drug administration orally or nasogastrically
